description: A small, bushy tree with 3 lobed leaves, with the central lobe being the longest and giving rise to the common name of trident maple. The yellow green small flowers, appear before the leaves in early spring. The leaves are bronze in spring, later becoming deep green with a grey underside in summer and then turn red and orange in autumn. Mature trees develop an attractive red-brown flaking bark.
aspect: East–facing or North–facing or South–facing or West–facing

description: A deciduous snakebark maple making a small tree with white-striped purple bark on the younger branches. Leaves oval on red stalks; little autumn colour. Flowers yellow in drooping racemes in spring
aspect: South–facing or North–facing or East–facing or West–facing

description: A medium-sized tree that has attractive green bark streaked with white and bright green foliage which turns yellow in autumn
aspect: South–facing or North–facing or West–facing or East–facing

description: A deciduous tree, to 25m or more in its native range, though often smaller in cultivation. Leaves are broad, shallowly 5-lobed, slightly glossy green, and often downy on the undersides. Clusters of small yellow flowers appear before the leaves in early spring, followed by winged seeds that are sometimes tinted silvery pink. Leaves turn yellow and rusty orange in autumn

A deciduous tree to around 12m high or more, with large, broadly oval green leaves that are heart-shaped at the base and serrated at the edges. Small spikes of yellow-green flowers are produced in spring, followed by winged fruits. Leaves turn rich amber yellow in autumn
A variable species with peeling, usually copper-brown or pinkish bark and dark green leaves up to 12cm long. In early spring it produces long, yellow-brown male catkins
aspect: South–facing or East–facing or North–facing or West–facing

description: A medium to large tree, to 30 metres, with thickish branches. It is distinguished by its almost black bark , which sheds in thick, small plates rather than peeling, and by its erect female catkins in spring. These show above the gracefully pointed, short stalked leaves
aspect: South–facing or North–facing or East–facing or West–facing

synonyms: Betula ermanii var. ermanii f. ganjuensis
description: Vigorous, graceful tree about 20m in height, sometimes multi-stemmed, with peeling pinkish or creamy-white bark on the trunk, papery brown bark on the branches; coarsely toothed, ovate, dark green leaves to 10cm long turn yellow in autumn; yellow-brown male catkins open with the leaves
aspect: South–facing or North–facing or West–facing or East–facing

description: A compact shrub, to 5m high, with conspicuously-pointed, glossy winter buds and upright branches when young, spreading with age. Glossy dark-green leaves turn yellow to yellow-brown in autumn and yellow brown male catkins, to 10cm long, are produced in spring
aspect: South–facing or North–facing or West–facing or East–facing

commonName: black birch, cherry birch, mahogany birch, mountain mahogany, wintergreen
description: A conical tree, to 15m tall, with dark-red bark that becomes dark-grey with age. Aromatic shoots produce yellow-green leaves, to 10cm long, that turn yellow in autumn. Yellow-brown male catkins, to 8cm long, appear in early spring
Find help & information on Prunus mexicana from the RHS
aspect: East–facing or North–facing or South–facing or West–facing

description: Find help & information on Prunus caroliniana | Carolina cherry laurel from the RHS
aspect: East–facing or North–facing or South–facing or West–facing

description: Find help & information on Prunus maackii | Manchurian cherry from the RHS
aspect: East–facing or North–facing or South–facing or West–facing

description: A medium, spreading, deciduous tree with double, pale pink flowers on long stems hanging below the branches in mid- to late spring. The leaves turn dark orange in autumn
aspect: East–facing or South–facing or North–facing or West–facing

description: A small, round-headed tree to 8m with mid-green foliage rounded at the base with a long, pointed tip. White or pink-tinged flowers up to 2cm across appear in early to mid-spring, before the leaves, followed by succulent, edible, red-tinged, yellow-orange fruit. Many cultivated varieties of apricot have been developed from this species.

A small, freely-flowering, deciduous tree, broadly conical in outline, with lightly-lobed dark green leaves. Flowers 5cm in width, white, opening from red buds and followed by fruit to 2.5cm in length, yellowish-orange or orange
aspect: South–facing or North–facing or East–facing or West–facing

description: A small tree with pendulous branches bearing bronze-green leaves, with red-purple flowers in spring, followed by small deep reddish-purple fruits
aspect: South–facing or North–facing or East–facing or West–facing

description: A small tree to 6m with a rounded crown and distinctive, lobed and toothed leaves with a woolly underside, turning orange and scarlet in autumn. Flat, pure white flowers in mid- to late spring are followed by small, egg-shaped, reddish-green fruit 1cm across, on long stalks

A deciduous tree, with reddish purple young shoots and broadly oval, bluntly toothed leaves that are flushed red when young, and mature to deep green. Dark red buds open to deep pink flowers in spring, followed in autumn by small, dark red fruits covered with a plum-purple bloom

A spreading, semi-weeping, deciduous shrub with arching branches, to about 2.5m high and 3m wide, and deeply lobed leaves. Fragrant white flowers open from pink buds in mid-spring, followed by small, red or yellow fruit
aspect: North–facing or West–facing or East–facing or South–facing

description: An upright deciduous tree with a rounded crown and large, slightly bluish leaves of around 15 leaflets,which turn yellow and orange in autumn. Heads of white flowers in mid-spring are followed by large clusters of orange-yellow berries
aspect: South–facing or North–facing or West–facing or East–facing

description: A large shrub or small tree 7-10m high, with a dense bushy habit, simple glossy green leaves, lobed towards the base, and dense clusters of white flowers in spring, followed by coral-red fruits which ripen in early summer but may then remain on the tree until midwinter
aspect: South–facing or North–facing or West–facing or East–facing

commonName: blunt-leaved Hupeh rowan, Hupeh rowan 'Pink Pagoda', rowan 'Pink Pagoda'
synonyms: Sorbus hupehensis var. obtusa C.K. Schneid.
description: A compact, medium-sized deciduous tree, around 4 to 8m in height, with blue-green pinnate foliage which changes to bright red and orange in the autumn. White flowers appear in spring, followed by large clusters or pink berries, turning to white. Will grow well in a container, and is pollution-tolerant and hardy in coastal conditions
aspect: South–facing or North–facing or West–facing or East–facing

description: A medium-sized deciduous tree, to 12m high, with a broad, dense canopy. Leaves are broadly oval, deeply-lobed and dark green. Clusters of white flowers in spring are followed by red berries in autumn
aspect: South–facing or North–facing or West–facing or East–facing

commonName: broad-leaved whitebeam, service tree of Fontainebleau
description: A resilient, round-headed tree up to 15m tall, with large, broad, tooth-edged leaves, greyish-white on the undersides. Clusters of small, creamy-white, five-petalled flowers appear in late spring or early summer followed in autumn by brownish-orange berries
aspect: East–facing or North–facing or South–facing or West–facing

description: A substantial deciduous tree, ultimately to 24m in height, with large leaves, 7.5-15cm long, deeply 7- sometimes 9-lobed, and coarsely toothed at the apex. Leaves are dark green above, paler beneath, both sides shining, becoming scarlet in autumn, the colour long-lasting. Flowers are yellow-green catkins, in spring. Acorns, if produced, to 2.5cm long and nearly as wide, partly enclosed in a deep, thin-edged cup

A spreading, deciduous tree to 20m tall with an oval to rounded crown and narrow, willow-like, glossy dark green leaves to 12cm long that turn yellow then brown in autumn. Insignificant flowers may be followed by small, rounded acorns in shallow, saucer-shaped cups
aspect: East–facing or North–facing or South–facing or West–facing

description: A spreading, deciduous tree to 20m tall, pyramidal before developing a broad, rounded crown with age. Oblong to lance-shaped, dark green glossy leaves up to 18cm long are unlobed with a slightly undulating edge and bristle-pointed; leaves turn yellow-brown to reddish-brown in autumn. Solitary, nearly spherical acorns are borne in scaly cups
aspect: East–facing or North–facing or South–facing or West–facing

commonName: American red oak, northern red oak
description: A fast-growing large deciduous tree with an open, spreading crown and broad leaves to 22cm in length, turning red or red-brown in autumn. Flowers greenish, inconspicuous

A small, spreading evergreen tree to around 10m. The leaves are long and broad, with teeth along the edges towards the tips. When new ones open in spring, they are coppery-red making a good contrast with the dark evergreen leaves.
aspect: East–facing or South–facing or North–facing or West–facing

description: Large, vigorous deciduous tree reaching 30m in height, with a broad, spreading crown. Leaves broadly elliptic, yellow-green in spring, rich golden copper to russet-brown in autumn. Small, green flowers in early spring, are followed by bristly fruits (nuts)
aspect: South–facing or West–facing or North–facing or East–facing

description: A very large, deciduous tree reaching 40m. It is extremely similar to European Beech, except may prove to be better suited to hotter drier climates. It has bright green leaves which cast thorough shade and on branches lower than 3-4m, keep its autumn orange-brown leaves all winter, only falling as new ones grow. This makes it a good hedge without being evergreen. The bark is silver-grey with a smooth surface. Some years (most years), large quantities of small prickly nut cases containing 3-cornered nuts, are produced
aspect: East–facing or North–facing or South–facing or West–facing

description: A slow-growing, medium deciduous tree up to 15m in height. The bark is a smooth silvery-grey and its leaves, as its name suggests, are large, up to 15cm long, green through the summer turning light yellow in autumn. The inconspicuous flowers become bristly-cased nuts in autumn.
aspect: East–facing or North–facing or South–facing or West–facing

description: Tall, conical-columnar deciduous tree, about 20-30m in height, becoming broader with age. Wavy-margined, glossy green leaves turn golden-brown in autumn. Flowers inconspicuous, fruit bristly
aspect: South–facing or North–facing or West–facing or East–facing

description: Slow-growing, deciduous tree about 10m tall, with an upright, branching habit. Wavy-margined, ferny leaves emerge bronze-purple in spring maturing to dark greenish-purple in summer before turning a golden orange-brown in autumn. Inconspicuous greenish-yellow flowers are followed by brown fruits in autumn
aspect: North–facing or West–facing or East–facing or South–facing

description: A deciduous shrub or small tree, with a spreading habit, thorny stems and small, lobed, glossy dark green leaves. Clusters of white flowers are produced in late spring or early summer, followed by yellowish berries in autumn

commonName: albespyne, bird eagles, draenen wen lefn, English hawthorn, may, quickset thorn, quickthorn, whitethorn
description: Rounded, thorny, deciduous tree about 8m tall, with glossy, shallowly-lobed mid-green leaves, and fllattened clusters of of white to pink flowers in late spring, followed by red fruit in early autumn
aspect: West–facing or South–facing or North–facing or East–facing

description: A deciduous shrub or small tree, with thorny stems and shallowly lobed, slightly hairy green leaves with serrated edges. Clusters of white flowers are produced in late spring and early summer, followed by red berries in autumn

A rounded, deciduous tree to about 10m in height, with thorny branches and glossy, deeply lobed dark green leaves, turning to gold in the autumn. Flat sprays of fragrant, creamy-white flowers with pink anthers, are produced in late spring, followed by plentiful dark red edible berries in autumn. The fruit can be made into jellies or used for making herbal tea (see harm notes for further details)
aspect: North–facing or East–facing or South–facing or West–facing

description: A small, spreading, thorny, deciduous tree to around 6m tall. Deeply-cut, dark green downy leaves with 5-9 lobes are grey beneath and turn yellow in the autumn. White fragrant flowers in rounded sprays of twelve or more are followed by aromatic red or yellowish-red fruits
aspect: West–facing or South–facing or North–facing or East–facing

description: A spreading, deciduous tree eventually reaching 25m in height, with broadly-ovate bright green leaves to 13cm long, softly downy on both surfaces and edged with bristle-like teeth, the leaves often emerge red-tinged, then turning yellow in autumn. Clusters of fragrant, creamy-white flowers are borne in late summer and early autumn

A large, broadly pyramidal deciduous tree to 30m in height. Erect branches are often pendent at their tips with white-felted shoots bearing rounded, sharply toothed leaves to 13cm long, dark green above, covered in a silvery-white felt beneath, turning yellow in autumn. Clusters of up to 10 very fragrant, small, white flowers, in summer

A tall, decidous lightly rounded tree to about 20m tall, with broad to almost triangular, glossy 3-lobed dark green leaves, greyish-green beneath, to 15cm long, dark crimson-red when emerging in spring, turning gold in autumn. In summer, widely-branched clusters of up to 32 fragrant yellow flowers are borne on long stalks

A fast-growing, broadly columnar, deciduous tree to 40m tall, with large asymmetric heart-shaped, slightly toothed leaves, dark green above, pale green and downy below, turning yellow in autumn. Pendent clusters of 3-5 fragrant pale yellow flowers appear in midsummer

commonName: American basswood, American linden, American whitewood, basswood, whitewood
description: A broadly conical decidous tree about 20-30m tall, the young bark smooth and grey, rough and corky when mature, with a domed crown and spreading branches bearing very large, broad dark green leaves to 30cm long, turning yellow-green in autumn. Fragrant pale yellow flowers in clusters of up to 20 flowers are borne in early summer
A spreading deciduous tree of elegant appearance, with glossy, prominently veined leaves and conspicuous green fruiting catkins turning pale brown with maturity
aspect: East–facing or South–facing or North–facing or West–facing

description: A large, broadly conicaltree with smooth grey bark. The narrowly oval, double-toothed leaves have prominent veins and are up to 27cm long. They emerge purple-bronze in spring, becoming olive-green. Pale green, papery catkins up to 30cm long appear in spring, gradually fading to tawny brown

commonName: charmille, European hornbeam, horn beech, horse beech, hurst beech, oestrywydden, white beech, yoke elm
description: A large deciduous tree developing a fluted grey trunk. Leaves 5-8cm long, ovate, conspicuously ribbed, turning yellow in autumn. Catkins open in spring, followed by hop-like fruiting catkins to 8cm. Good for woodland settings
aspect: East–facing or South–facing or North–facing or West–facing

description: A small rounded deciduous tree with prominently veined ovate leaves, reddish when young and orange-tinted in autumn, and conspicuous fruiting racemes
aspect: North–facing or South–facing or West–facing or East–facing

description: Find help & information on Carpinus viminea from the RHS

Species evergreen shrub or tree eventually reaching 7m in height, larger in warm climates. Silvery-grey bark and olive-green young branches bearing leathery, glossy, dark green oblong-shaped leaves with small teeth on the margins. Flowers in late spring are creamy-white followed by red berries on female plants if pollinated by a male holly

Large deciduous, spreading shrub or small tree to about 9m in height, with mid-green leaves, and fragrant, pure white flowers, goblet-shaped at first, then opening to broad, thick and fleshy tepals, appearing in spring before the leaves

An upright, deciduous tree or large shrub reaching approximately 5m in height with ovate mid-green leaves to 15cm. The scented, tulip-shaped flowers, produced in spring, are a pale orangey-pink and creamy coloured on the inside; the flowers become floppy over time.
Deciduous large shrub or small tree about 6m tall, producing very large, pure white, cup-and-saucer-shaped flowers, up to 25cm across, in early spring before the leaves
A compact, upright, deciduous tree about 6m tall, with oblong to elliptic mid-green leaves. Flowering at an early age, the rich yellow flowers with red stamens are freely produced in early spring

A compact, deciduous shrub about 3-4m tall, with oval mid-green leaves to 15cm long, and deep reddish-purple buds opening in mid spring to fragrant, cupped flowers with usually 6 tepals, deep red-purple outside, pink within

A bushy upright deciduous shrub to 3m, with purple young shoots, bloomed white in winter, narrow oblong bright green leaves, glaucous beneath, and grey catkins to 2.5cm long with red anthers in early or mid spring before the leaves

A slow-growing, upright deciduous shrub or small tree, with reddish-brown stems and oval-shaped, finely toothed, deep green leaves with conspicuous veins. Slender yellow-green catkins emerge from red buds in spring
A suckering deciduous shrub with bristly branches bearing pinnate leaves with oval leaflets, and short racemes of deep rose-pink flowers 3cm long in late spring and early summer

commonName: bastard acacia, black locust, common robinia, fragrant white locust, locust, yellow locust
description: A fast-growing, spreading tree to 25m tall with deeply furrowed rough bark and spines formed from stipules on twigs and suckers. The dark green leaves comprise 5-11 pairs of oval leaflets. Dense, drooping clusters of slightly scented white flowers, each 15-20mm long and with a yellow blotch at the base of the standard petal, are borne in late spring and summer and are followed in autumn by hairless, linear to oblong pods containing 4-10 seeds
aspect: North–facing or West–facing or South–facing or East–facing

description: A bushy, upright, medium-sized deciduous tree with bright greenish-yellow, pinnate leaves, which become more vivid in summer and turn orange-yellow in autumn. Seldom flowers freely
aspect: West–facing or East–facing or South–facing or North–facing

description: A bushy, medium-sized deciduous tree which on maturity begins to branch horizontally, forming a spherical shape. Bright golden-yellow, pinnate leaves become vivid greenish-yellow in summer and orange-yellow in autumn. Seldom flowers freely
aspect: East–facing or North–facing or South–facing or West–facing

description: A small, deciduous tree to 10m if left unpruned, but otherwise usually 4-5m. The leaves are green with many pairs of rounded leaflets which turn yellow in autumn. Tolerant of pollution so makes a good urban courtyard specimen
aspect: East–facing or North–facing or South–facing or West–facing

commonName: balm of Gilead (of the Bible), liquid storax, lordwood
description: A slow-growing, large shrub or bushy tree with five-lobed, palmate leaves turning red, yellow and orange in autumn. Inconspicuous green flowers are followed by spiky, spherical seed clusters that persist into winter

A broadly conical, medium-sized tree to about 15m. Leaves are bright green, with three to five pointed lobes; young foliage is flushed red for much of the growing season but there is little autumn colour. Inconspicuous clusters of small, yellow-green flowers are followed by long-lasting, hanging, spiky, dark brown fruit

A deciduous tree to about 15m tall, broadly conical in outline. The 3-lobed leaves, turn to shades of red, orange and purple in autumn. Insignificant flowers in late spring are followed by spiky fruit capsules in autumn, which can remain on the tree into winter. Less hardy than other Liquidambars, requires a sheltered spot.

commonName: American red gum, American sweet gum, bilsted, copalm balsam, red gum, satin walnut
description: A deciduous tree to 20m tall, broadly conical in outline, with rather glossy, maple-like, 5 to 7-lobed leaves which turn to shades of orange, crimson and purple in autumn

A large, hardy and narrow, pyramid-shaped deciduous tree with glossy green star-shaped leaves which turn to brilliant shades of purple, red, yellow and orange in the autumn. A variety suited to large parks and large residential gardens
An neat-growing, bushy evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and growing to a height of 2-3m. For several months over summer, bears blue and white flowers in clusters followed by blue berries
aspect: North–facing or East–facing or West–facing or South–facing

description: A vigorous, large deciduous shrub climbing by aerial roots, with slender-pointed, ovate, entire leaves to 17cm in length. Flowers inconspicuous but surrounded by showy white ovate bracts to 9cm in length
aspect: South–facing or North–facing or East–facing or West–facing

description: A variable species, from mid sized shrubs to small trees, and up to around 5m high in cultivation. Leaves are dark green with greyish-white hairy undersides, usually toothed and often held on reddish stems. Produces broad flat flower heads from late spring to early summer, with loose clusters of small true flowers surrounded by larger florets, usually white but sometimes turning pink as they mature

A low-growing, compact deciduous shrub to around 100cm in height with ovate, dark green foliage. Clusters of blue to pink lacecap flowers are surrounded by white sterile ones and appear throughout the summer
A large self-clinging, deciduous climber with broadly oval leaves turning yellow in autumn. Flower-heads to 20cm in width, with small fertile flowers surrounded by showy white sterile ones
aspect: East–facing or North–facing or South–facing or West–facing

description: A vigorous large deciduous shrub which can be trained into a small tree, with arching branches bearing narrow, grey-green leaves and sweetly scented lilac-purple flowers, borne in clusters along the previous year's shoots

Deciduous shrub, around 3m in height, with oval, deeply toothed, leaves fragrant when young, and arching stems covered in dense, white felt. Racemes of fragrant, small, pale lavender-pink flowers, with a white eye, produced from mid to late summer

Semi-evergreen to evergreen shrub about 2.5m tall, with dark green leaves, strongly felted grey-white beneath. Pale mauve-pink, yellow-eyed, strongly fragrant flowers produced in arching panicles, through winter into early spring.
Find help & information on Buddleja yunnanensis | Yunnan butterfly bush from the RHS
A bushy, evergreen shrub, up to 2m tall with lance-shaped, rough, dark green leaves. The clusters of scented, small creamy flowers are produced in summer.

commonName: crampbark, cranberry, dog eller, dog rowan, European cranberry bush, European cranberry tree, gatten, gatten tree, marsh alder, ople tree, red elder, rose elder, snowball tree, water elder, whitten tree
description: A vigorous, bushy, deciduous shrub to 5m, with maple-like, palm-shaped, lobed, dark green leaves, tinted red in autumn. Flat clusters of lacecap-like flowers, composed of tubular white fertile flowers surrounded by larger white sterile flowers appear in late spring and early summer, followed by translucent bright red fruits, often persisting into winter
aspect: North–facing or West–facing or South–facing or East–facing

description: A multi-stemmed, upright to spreading, deciduous shrub to 4m tall. The pointed, ovate-lanceolate to oblong, slightly-toothed leaves are up to 12cm long and change in colour from blue-green to dark-green in spring and summer before taking on attractive autumnal hues. Small white flowers borne in early summer are followed by orange-yellow berries that turn a brilliant red in autumn
aspect: South–facing or North–facing or East–facing or West–facing

commonName: American arrow wood, arrow wood, southern arrow wood
description: A deciduous shrub to 3m high, with an upright, arching habit and thin, ovate to rounded, toothed green leaves that turn yellow and red in autumn. Broad, flat clusters of very small, tubular white flowers are produced in late spring and early summer. These are followed by small, ovoid blue-black berries in autumn and winter

A dense, bushy, deciduous shrub, to 2m high and wide, with ovate, toothed dark-green leaves, up to 10cm long, that often turn red in autumn. Rounded clusters of white, fragrant flowers emerge from pink buds in spring and are followed by black fruits
aspect: North–facing or East–facing or South–facing or West–facing

commonName: American black haw, black haw, sheepberry
description: A large deciduous shrub or small tree, to around 4m high in cultivation, though can reach up to 8m. Leaves are oval-shaped and glossy green with serrated edges. Broad, flat-topped clusters of small white flowers are produced in mid to late spring, followed by relatively large, edible blue-black berries. Leaves turn shades of red and purple in autumn
A bushy, upright, evergreen shrub with dark green leaves and single, scented, white flowers with notched petals in late winter

A slow-growing, tender, large, upright evergreen shrub, with dark-green, lance-shaped, toothed leaves. It has fragrant, white, single flowers with many golden-yellow stamens in autumn and winter. If you drink tea, black, or green, this is the plant it comes from. Commercially grown plants are pruned to a height of 1.2m, to facilitate picking

A robust, compact rounded evergreen shrub to 1m tall. Wavy-margined flowers, white flushed pink, with some maroon spotting on the upper lobe, open from deep pink buds in early and mid spring. Very floriferous
A semi-dwarf evergreen shrub to 1m, producing trusses of 3-4 scented, white flowers, flushed with pink when in bud, in April.
aspect: East–facing or North–facing or South–facing or West–facing

description: A large, narrow, evergreen tree, with dark green leaves, to 20cm long, a smooth cinnamon-brown, fawn or silvery indumentum on the undersides. Flowers, produced in rounded trusses in early spring, are up to 5cm long and may be red, white or any shade of pink, usually with spotting in the throat
aspect: South–facing or North–facing or West–facing or East–facing

description: A large, evergreen shrub or small tree to 5m tall, with glossy, dark green leaves to 3cm long, and small, yellowish flowers in clusters, produced in the leaf axils during spring
aspect: East–facing or South–facing or North–facing or West–facing

commonName: Balearic boxwood, Balearic Islands box, giant box tree, Minorca box
description: A vigorous, upright, evergreen shrub or small tree to 3m tall, with leathery, glossy, bright-green leaves to 4cm long, and small clusters of yellowish flowers in spring
Find help & information on Buxus 'Green Gem' from the RHS
A large, upright, deciduous shrub with mid-green foliage and clusters of heavily scented, bowl-shaped, cream-white flowers appearing in early summer
aspect: East–facing or South–facing or North–facing or West–facing

description: An upright, deciduous shrub native to W. China and S.E. Tibet, growing to 3-4m tall, with slender, toothed, dark green foliage and fragrant, pure white flowers with purple calyxes appearing in summer
aspect: East–facing or North–facing or South–facing or West–facing

description: Find help & information on Forsythia ovata | Korean forsythia from the RHS

commonName: golden bells, Japanese golden bell tree
description: A deciduous, arching shrub to 3m tall and wide. Slender shoots bear nodding, narrowly-trumpet-shaped, yellow flowers, up to 3cm across, in spring before the leaves appear. Leaves are usually undivided but may occasionally be three-lobed
A compact, deciduous, spreading shrub to 0.75m high with purple-tinged, dark green, oval leaves. Lightly fragrant, dark pink flowers with yellow throats are borne in late spring and early summer

Bushy deciduous shrub to about 3m tall, with hairy branches, elliptic, almost stalkless mid to dark green leaves, and funnel-shaped flowers, yellow-green in bud becoming pink to lavender as they age, produced from mid spring to early summer

an upright, deciduous shrub with bright green leaves and bell-shaped, pale yellow flowers in late spring to early summer,often with conspicuous throat markings that vary from light yellow-orange to dark orange-red
aspect: North–facing or West–facing or East–facing or South–facing

description: A large, upright, deciduous shrub about 2m or more tall, with oval dark green leaves and large, funnel-shaped purple-red flowers produced in masses during late spring and early summer
A deciduous, spreading shrub to 2.5m tall and wide with arching stems and oval, toothed, bright green leaves.Pure white, tubular flowers are borne from late spring into early summer
Find help & information on Choisya palmeri from the RHS
A rounded, medium-sized bushy evergreen shrub, with dark, glossy green leaves divided into three broad leaflets. Flowers pure white, scented, often appearing fitfully into winter
Find help & information on Choisya dumosa from the RHS

A small evergreen shrub with an open rounded habit and bright green leaves composed of 3-5 slender leaflets. Fragrant flowers to 3cm in width are white, tinged pink in bud, and appear in small clusters in late spring, and again in autumn

A free-flowering, bushy, evergreen shrub. The aromatic leaves, with three to five slender leaflets, open yellow, maturing to green. Clusters of fragrant, white flowers appear in late spring and again in late summer to autumn
A spreading, evergreen shrub to about 1.5m high and 2.5m across. It has small, dark green leaves and rounded, terminal clusters of dark blue flowers in mid- to late spring
Fast-growing, bushy, evergreen shrub to 3m tall and 5m wide with oblong, glossy, deep green leaves to 2.5cm long, and panicles to 6cm long of deep blue flowers in mid and late spring

A clump-forming, herbaceous perennial up to 90cm in height, with strawberry-like dark green leaves composed of five broad leaflets. Branched, red-tinged stems bear loose clusters of dark red or dark pink flowers 2.5cm in width, throughout summer
A rounded deciduous shrub with slender arching shoots bearing small lance-shaped leaves and clusters of small white flowers on short lateral shoots all along the branches in spring
aspect: East–facing or South–facing or North–facing or West–facing

description: Graceful, widespreading deciduous shrub about 1.8m tall, with slender arching branches and 3-lobed or deeply toothed green leaves, pale grey-green beneath. White flowers in rounded clusters appear all along the stems, in early summer
A dense, bushy deciduous shrub about 1.5m tall, with narrow light green leaves to 4cm in length. White flowers 6mm in width are borne in abundant small clusters along the branches, in early spring
aspect: East–facing or South–facing or North–facing or West–facing

description: A species of compact, evergreen shrub with dark green, glossy foliage and clusters of strongly fragranced creamy-white flowers in spring

A slow-growing evergreen shrub to 2m high, with an open habit and aromatic leathery green leaves, held in clusters at the tips of the stems. Small, rounded clusters of yellow-green flowers are produced in spring. Plants in this species can be male or female; in female plants, pollinated flowers are followed by bright red berries in the autumn

A variable, evergreen, densely-branched, dome-shaped shrub, low and creeping or erect, from 0.5m to 7m in height (but typically up to 1.5m in cultivation), with slightly-aromatic, dark green, leathery, obovate to elliptic leaves. White flowers in spring, sometimes flushed pink or red on the outside, appear in panicles at the ends of branches; male flowerheads are large and conspicuous, up to 8cm long, and very sweetly-scented, while the smaller fragrant female flowerheads are followed, if pollinated, by brilliantly bright red fruits, 8mm across, which usually last until the next flowers appear the following spring

description: An upright, bushy evergreen shrub with leathery, dark green foliage and clusters of small, slightly fragrant, star-shaped pinkish white flowers in spring

commonName: holly-leaved barberry, mountain grape, Rocky Mountain grape, Tall Oregon grape
description: A vigorous, low-spreading, evergreen shrub with glossy green, slightly prickly leaves becoming purplish in winter. Large clusters of yellow flowers appear in spring, followed by black berries
aspect: South–facing or North–facing or West–facing or East–facing

description: An upright, evergreen shrub to 2m tall, with large, dark green leathery pinnate leaves to 45cm long, with up to 19 sharp-toothed, slender leaflets, and small, fragrant pale yellow flowers in spreading or drooping sprays to 25cm long, from late autumn to early spring, followed by blue-black berries
aspect: North–facing or West–facing or East–facing or South–facing

description: A large, bushy evergreen shrub to a height of up to 8m with slender, dark shoots and glossy oval light green leaves. Small, fragrant pale yellow flowers are borne in clusters in summer

A dense, broad, slow-growing medium-sized evergreen shrub with leathery, glossy, obovate leaves, and large terminal umbels of small sweetly-scented flowers opening white, soon turning yellow, in late spring and early summer

A large, broadly columnar evergreen shrub with slender, dark shoots. Leaves rounded, glossy light green, with wavy margins. Small, honey-scented deep purple flowers open in clusters in late spring and early summer

description: Find help & information on Pittosporum undulatum | Australian laurel from the RHS

A clump-forming herbaceous perennial, 45-90cm high, with deciduous, deeply seven-lobed green leaves, and flowers, up to 2cm across, of widely-spaced pale lilac petals with darker violet veins and pink stigmas, in early summer
aspect: South–facing or North–facing or West–facing or East–facing

description: A spreading, mound-forming perennial to about 0.5m high and 1m across. The yellow-green leaves are deeply-lobed. The flowers, borne in pairs all summer, are red-purple with dark veining and a very dark eye
aspect: South–facing or North–facing or West–facing or East–facing

description: A rhizomatous perennial forming a compact mat of foliage which may colour well in autumn, with white-eyed, light blue flowers 4-6cm wide in summer, often again in autumn
aspect: South–facing or North–facing or West–facing or East–facing

description: A herbaceous perennial forming a large clump of lobed leaves, tinted red in autumn. Flowers 4cm in width, magenta-crimson with black centres, on upright stems to 1.2m
aspect: South–facing or North–facing or West–facing or East–facing

description: A bushy sub-shrub, reaching 1m tall, with aromatic green foliage. Bicoloured, creamy-yellow and peach, flowers are borne in terminal racemes from mid-summer into autumn
A bushy evergreen shrub, 60-90cm high, with mid to deep-green, aromatic leaves. Salmon-pink flowers are borne in profusion, in terminal racemes, over a long period from early summer to autumn
A compact perennial with fragrant, mid-green lance shaped foliage and slender spikes of abundant pale purple-pink lipped flowers in summer.
A semi-evergreen, upright, tall and bushy perennial which has green, long, lance-shaped leaves and whorls of long tubular velvety pink flowers that are often curved in late summer and autumn.

A small, slow-growing, mat-forming species of evergreen to semi-evergreen perennial to around 20cm in height, forming a mound of aromatic, silvery-green, soft, ferny, deeply lobed foliage which turns almost white in periods of drought. Clusters of pure white, multi-petalled flowers, appear from April to June. A great addition to rock and alpine gardens and borders and drought-tolerant once established. Attracts bees, butterflies and other beneficial insects

commonName: flossflower, sweet maudlin, sweet milfoil, sweet Nancy, sweet yarrow
description: A clump-forming perennial to 80cm tall with green, divided or shallowly-toothed leaves to 5cm long and many small flowerheads made up of clusters of tiny yellow flowers in summer
A clump-forming perennial up to 90cm tall with divided, fern-like, aromatic foliage and flattened clusters of pale yellow flowers produced in summer

A tall, clump-forming perennial to 40-100cm tall, with coarsely divided ferny green leaves. Branched, upright stems bear terminal clusters of small, white flowers with recurved petals and yellow centres, appearing in the summer
A low-growing, spreading, semi-evergreen perennial with divided, grey-green foliage and flat-topped clusters of small, creamy-white flowers borne on upright stems in summer
A simple yet stunning coneflower variety producing melon-yellow flowers with an orange central cone. Excellent as a cut flower, for growing in containers and for attracting pollinators

A perennial species, about 1.2m tall, with hairy linear mid-green leaves. Distinctive pale pink flowers with long and linear ray petals, reflexed to droop down, surround a central orange-brown cone and appear from midsummer to early autumn. A great choice for prairie planting

Spreading perennial coneflower about 1m tall, with narrow leaves to 20cm long, and daisy-like flowerheads with narrow, drooping golden-yellow rays to 7cm long, surrounding a conical central brown cone, flowering from midsummer to early autumn; native to prairies of south-central USA

A clump-forming, herbaceous perennial to 90cm with strong, branched, upright stems bearing rough, hairy leaves. The flower-heads, produced from mid-summer to mid-autumn have clear yellow outer petals and a greenish-bronze cone

Solitary flowerheads to 12cm across with slightly reflexed, light purplish-pink rays and a golden brown central disk, appear from midsummer to autumn; native to prairies and woods of eastern USA

Find help & information on Hylotelephium 'Winky' | stonecrop 'Winky' from the RHS

aspect: South–facing or North–facing or West–facing or East–facing

description: A slowly-spreading, deciduous sub-shrub with dark brown stems and green, heart-shaped leaves with wavy edges. Clusters of small, scented, star-shaped flowers, white tinged with pink, appear in late summer and early autumn

description: A variable, bushy annual up to around 80cm high, with palmate leaves divided into up to 9 narrow leaflets. Stems and leaf undersides are coated with fine downy hairs. Upright spikes of pea-like flowers, in shades from white to deep blue, are produced in early summer, and followed by seeds which can be edible when processed correctly
Find help & information on Lupinus 'Saffron' from the RHS
An unusual, upright, clump-forming perennial to around 90cm tall with glossy, star-shaped green foliage. Lavender-blue flowers appear on upright spikes from June to September
An erect perennial with spikes to 65cm long, and numerous side branches, bearing semi-double pale cream flowers 7cm across, with grey-brown eyes
Find help & information on Delphinium 'Butterball' from the RHS

An evergreen, sparingly-branched shrub, to 1.5m in height, with serrated, oval, dark green leaves. Flowers are foxglove-like with a flattened appearance, reddish-orange or apricot in colour and held on upright spikes to 30cm in length

A compact, semi-evergreen perennial, to around 30cm high in flower, with a woody base and wrinkled green leaves covered with long silver-grey hairs, mostly clustered at the base of the plant. Upright spikes bearing small, nodding, tubular flowers, usually pink but sometimes white and with purplish spots inside, are produced from spring to late summer

A clump-forming, herbaceous perennial to 60cm tall, with a branching habit and hairy dark green leaves. Tall spikes produce masses of tubular pink flowers with spotted throats, with a long flowering season through summer from June through to August
aspect: East–facing or North–facing or South–facing or West–facing

description: A rosette-forming perennial to 1m tall, producing a basal clump of oval, dark green leaves, with erect leafy stems bearing loose racemes of brown-veined, light yellow flowers 3.5cm long in summer

aspect: South–facing or North–facing or West–facing or East–facing

An herbaceous perennial to 1.4m tall with upright stems clothed in aromatic, ovate, toothed leaves to 7.5cm long. In summer, long terminal spikes of pale whitish flowers spotted with purple open from very pale yellow buds

A compact perennial with narrow, greyish-green leaves to 3cm long. Short spikes, to 40cm high, of white flowers tinted with pale blue are produced from summer into early autumn

A bushy, clump-forming deciduous perennial with aromatic grey-green foliage and upright spikes of violet-blue flowers which are produced from summer through until the autumn. A hardy variety that is also attractive to cats

Vigorous, clump-forming perennial about 45cm tall, with dark green, deeply dissected leaves, and bearing vivid lavender-pink flower plumes to 30cm tall, above the foliage during summer

A clump-forming, semi-evergreen to evergreen perennial bearing lobed, rounded, red-pink leaves with a slivery sheen and slender, wiry, dark red stems bearing open panicles of pink flowers from late spring into autumn.

A compact, clump-forming semi-evergreen to evergreen herbaceous perennial producing silvery foliage with black veining and pale purple undersides. Masses of fuchsia-pink flowers appear on long stems above the foliage throughout the spring and summer
aspect: East–facing or North–facing or South–facing or West–facing

description: Find help & information on Heuchera 'Beaujolais' | alum root 'Beaujolais' from the RHS
aspect: East–facing or North–facing or South–facing or West–facing

aspect: East–facing or North–facing or South–facing or West–facing

aspect: South–facing or West–facing or East–facing or North–facing

Clusters of two to eight, bell-shaped, papery-textured flowers, 5-6cm across, are white at first, fading through pale pink to green, often with conspicuous dark veins, are borne in early spring

This species is native to Japan and Korea, and is a little more distinctive and attractive than some of our native UK hederas

a vigorous deciduous climber with pinnate leaves and, in early summer, fragrant, pea-like, violet-blue, pink or white flowers in racemes to 30cm or longer
a large deciduous climber with twining stems, dark green, pinnate leaves and drooping racemes to 30cm in length, of fragrant, mauve or lilac-coloured flowers opening before the leaves

A medium-sized deciduous shrub with long, arching branches. Leaves small, trifoliate. Flowers to 2.5cm in width, bright yellow in winter and spring

Find help & information on Passiflora holosericea from the RHS

commonName: American hop, bine, bines, European hop, hopysen

A vigorous climber with mid to dark green leaves comprising of seven to nine leaflets. From late summer to autumn produces terminal clusters of dark orange to red, trumpet-shaped flowers

A compact, clump-forming, bulbous perennial to 25cm tall with tufts of thread-like leaves to 1mm wide. Up to twelve star-shaped, pink-purple flowers are borne in loose umbels in summer

Bulbous perennial to 1m in height, with long, strap-shaped grey-green leaves, dying back at flowering time, and dense rounded clusters of starry light lavender-purple flowers, to 20cm across, borne on strong, straight stems in early summer

Bulbous perennial producing broad, strap-shaped mid-green leaves, and straight stems to 50cm tall, bearing heads of pink flowers which are initially densely packed, but become lax when the flower stalks lengthen as the flowers mature, they appear in mid and late summer
Bulbous perennial, to 80cm tall, with strap-shaped leaves. ln summer, upright stems bear large globular umbels up to 12cm in diameter comprising deep purple, star-shaped flowers

Vigorous, clump-forming bulbous perennial to 60cm tall, with narrow, strap-shaped leaves and erect stems, nodding at the tips and bearing up to 40 umbels of bell-shaped mid to deep pink flowers in summer
A small, perennial corm growing to around 5cm high, with long, narrow green leaves with a paler central stripe. Produces rounded, golden yellow or orange flowers in late winter and early spring
